questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 72°. What is the alternate angle on the other parallel line?
questions.why: Alternate angles are equal — they sit on opposite sides of the transversal between the parallel lines, forming a 'Z' shape. 108° would be the co-interior (allied) angle instead.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has angles of 50°, 60°, and 70°. What type of triangle is this?
questions.why: All three angles are different, so all three sides are different lengths, making it scalene. Isosceles needs two equal angles, and equilateral needs all three equal.

questions.subject: Maths

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In human reproduction, where does fertilisation normally take place?
questions.why: The egg is released from the ovary and travels down the fallopian tube, where sperm usually meets and fertilises it. The uterus is where the fertilised egg later implants, not where fertilisation happens.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which religious group launched the First Crusade in 1096 to try to capture Jerusalem?
questions.why: The First Crusade was called by the Pope and fought mainly by knights and soldiers from Western Europe, aiming to take Jerusalem from Muslim control. The Byzantines asked for help but weren't the main crusading force.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A historian writes: 'The king raised taxes heavily, which led to widespread rebellion across the country.' Which part of this sentence describes the cause?
questions.why: The cause is the event that triggers what follows — here, the tax rise leads to the rebellion (the consequence). Students often muddle which half is which when the sentence is reordered.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Magna Carta 1215 was originally created to address a conflict between King John and which group?
questions.why: Magna Carta was forced on King John by his own barons, angry about high taxes and abuses of power. It wasn't a peasant document — ordinary people gained little from it directly at the time.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student tests how the number of hours spent revising affects exam scores. They make sure every student uses the same textbook. What is the controlled variable?
questions.why: The controlled variable is what's kept the SAME so it doesn't affect the results unfairly — here, the textbook. Hours revising is what's changed (independent), and exam scores is what's measured (dependent).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 130°. What is the vertically opposite angle to it?
questions.why: Vertically opposite angles are always equal, formed when two lines cross. 50° would be the angle that's supplementary (adds to 180°), not vertically opposite.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A quadrilateral has two pairs of parallel sides and all four sides equal in length, but its angles are not right angles. What is the most specific name for it?
questions.why: A rhombus has all sides equal and opposite sides parallel, but the angles don't have to be 90°. Calling it a square would be wrong since a square needs right angles too.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: During asexual reproduction, how genetically similar is the offspring compared to the single parent?
options: Only similar in appearance, not DNA
questions.why: Asexual reproduction involves only one parent and no mixing of genetic material, so offspring are genetically identical clones. Sexual reproduction is the one that mixes DNA from two parents, giving variation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Your classmate says: 'In an experiment testing how the amount of water affects plant growth, the plant's height is the independent variable because it's the main thing in the experiment.' Using a different example of your own, explain what actually makes a variable 'independent' versus 'dependent', and correct the misunderstanding in your classmate's reasoning.
